summary: GET one https url and write the bytes to the output, optionally only a window of it. The host must be one the ops pack names; the url is checked again on every redirect hop.

parity.note: The whole-file path writes the origin's bytes verbatim, so it is bit_exact by construction. The windowed path is an ffmpeg `-c copy` remux — no re-encode, no scaler, no rate control — and is deterministic for a fixed ffmpeg build, the same condition media.scale states: the pinned BUILD, not the box. tests/test_op_media_fetch.py asserts the argv is a pure function of (url, path, seconds), so a drift shows as an argv diff in milliseconds rather than as different bytes after a fetch. FAILURE: `dst` is OPTIONAL — a dead origin leaves no file instead of raising, because one chain carries a whole batch of candidates and a raising handler would let one dead url kill every sibling. The CALLER decides whether a missing file is fatal; a batch of siblings must not die for one dead address.

url.description: The ORIGIN to fetch. A LOCATION, never a decision: it carries no threshold and no editorial rule, and this op has no vocabulary for what the bytes are for. It is a param rather than an input binding so that the host allowlist can live in the ops pack, at the one place a third-party url is dereferenced — an input url is fetched by the runner before any handler exists, which would push the check into podagent/cp.py (submodule commit, image rebuild) and hide `needs: [net]` from the placement gate. The brain refuses to bind a credential-carrying url (op_backend.assert_bindable_origin); the pod refuses to fetch an unlisted host (montyops.stock_hosts). Both, on purpose.

window_seconds.description: Pull only N seconds of the file, starting at `seek_seconds` (default 0). A BYTE WINDOW on the file's own axis. Omit for the whole file. Measured on both keyed providers: ftyp+moov sit at the front and the CDNs serve Range, so a pexels 4K/57s master costs 12.6 MB for 5 s instead of 137.3 MB.

seek_seconds.description: Where the window STARTS on the file's own axis. Was refused on the grounds that a prefix cannot disclose where in a clip anything is cut — and that refusal cost whole masters: 30 winners on one fixture are 1642 MB to play 2.4 s each (839 s fetched, ~72 s used, 11.7x). What it discloses is ONE number: somebody wanted this url starting around here. No intent, no score, no threshold, no rank, no beat, nothing that says a moment was CHOSEN or that distinguishes a winner from a candidate — the same class of fact as a duration or a geometry, arriving already collapsed into a number. No selection RULE crosses. The handler guarantees the delivered file PRESENTS from this offset (input `-ss` + mp4 edit list; a degrade re-trims locally rather than silently shipping a file that starts at 0), because the caller records it as the clip's origin and seeks relative to it.

window_policy.description: When present, `window_seconds` is mandatory and the transport may deliver only that window. The small-object whole-body optimisation and the whole-file retry after a failed Range/remux are forbidden: the step fails without a `dst`, so the caller can try another rendition/source. Omit for adaptive fetches such as cheap low-resolution rank previews, whose measured small-object whole-body path remains valid.
